The Sopranos (1999) - “Pax Soprana” (Season 1, Episode 6) 

In one of the most Iconic endings to an episode, we see the DiMeo crime family throw a banquet to honor Uncle Junior being named the new boss. Unknowingly to them, the FBI infiltrates the party by posing as waiters. The undercover agents use hidden cameras disguised as buttons on their name tags to snap photos of every mobster at the table. The scene famously ends with the photos being delivered to the FBI office, where agents update their criminal hierarchy board.

source_details.synopsis: The Sopranos is an American crime drama television series created by David Chase for HBO. The series follows Tony Soprano (James Gandolfini), a New Jersey Mafia boss. Suffering from panic attacks, he reluctantly begins seeing psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Melfi (Lorraine Bracco), who encourages him to open up about his difficulties balancing his family life with his criminal activities. Other important characters include Tony's family, Mafia colleagues, and rivals, most notably his wife Carmela (Edie Falco), his nephew and protégé Christopher Moltisanti (Michael Imperioli), and his uncle Corrado "Junior" Soprano (Dominic Chianese).
